subject: Dedicated capacity: Thermogenix memory, KV routing, and quantization playbook
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@thermogenix.com>, support+it@thermogenix.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: Thermogenix memory, KV routing, and quantization playbook

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. I drafted a concise plan focused on two closely related risks you flagged: long-context memory footprint (KV cache) and the downstream impact of quantizing model weights for cost savings. The attached spreadsheet has the telemetry slice you sent plus a couple of run-rate assumptions; summary below.

Top-line ask from Thermogenix: a dedicated pool to support interactive product search + long-form summarization. Peak concurrency target: 90 concurrent sessions, median session length ~ 7 turns, 40% of sessions ask for 32k context pages, 60% 8–16k. Token distribution is spiky — 5% of calls hit >20k prompt tokens.

Immediate recommendations (high level):
- Reserve a baseline pool sized for 90 steady concurrent sessions on the production model variant (we recommend a 70B-compatible variant for your quality bar).
- Use routing policies: prefer float16 high-precision instances for real-time critical routes, auto-fallback to an aggressively quantized 4-bit variant for non-blocking batch or background tasks.
- Provision ~2x headroom for burst windows and canary/upgrade transitions.

Key numbers from the estimator (see attachments):
- Model weights (float16) baseline: ~140GB. 4-bit quant variant: roughly ~35GB (estimate depends on quant scheme + group size).
- KV cache sizing: 32k context KV contributions add ~10–14GB of GPU memory per replica at float16 (model-specific variance). For 8–16k contexts it's ~3–7GB.
- Combined working set (weights + peak KV): float16 70B with 32k -> ~154GB (so needs 2x 80GB-class GPUs or offload/partitioning). Quantized 4-bit variant with same KV -> ~50GB + 14GB KV ≈ 64GB (fits on a single 80GB GPU in many cases).

Operational/routing notes:
- We can configure a routing policy that pins low-latency product-search traffic to float16 nodes (SLO target < 250ms median) and sends heavy summarization / large-context requests to the quantized pool with queued or batched execution.
- KV sharing/caching: recommend aggressive prefix caching for repeated product context (reduces KV pressure by ~20–30% based on your sample).

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal sizing review with our infra folks — Marcus/Karthik, can you validate headroom math and recommend pod topology?
2) Thermogenix to confirm acceptable quality risk for 4-bit fallback on non-interactive routes.
3) If green, we finalize a Dedicated estimate and a short pilot window (2 weeks) to collect live KV usage.

Attachments: thermogenix_kv_profile.xlsx (telemetry slice), redwood-dedicated-estimate-THER-2027.pdf (ballpark pricing + pool config).

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet — that layout helps. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Product-search traffic is latency-sensitive and must stay below 300ms P50. We can tolerate up to 800ms for background summarization jobs.
- On the quality tradeoff: our ML team is ok with a small measurable delta for background tasks, but customer-facing search must match current F1 baseline within 1–2%.
- We do intend to push more long-context requests over time (legal docs ingestion) so the 32k tail is important.

Question: in your numbers you show combined working set for float16 70B + 32k exceeds 140GB. Would a multi-GPU sharded approach be the preferred path for product-search to avoid the quantized variant for that route?

Also looped in our infra alias (support+it) for any network/KMS questions.

1) A short note on pod topology options that meet P50 <300ms for product-search with 32k tail. Options we should include: (A) multi-GPU sharded replicas (A100/H100 80GB pairs, NCCL/sharding); (B) model- and KV-partitioning with NVMe offload for KV; (C) smaller single-GPU with reduced context + front-door routing to fallback to longer-job queue. Provide pros/cons and rough 90-concurrency commitments.

2) A recommended quantization deployment pattern: how to maintain canary/fallback logic (e.g., run 10% traffic to float16 during rollout, automatic rollback on quality signals). Include expected memory numbers per-replica for the three contexts (8k, 16k, 32k) across float16 / 4-bit FP variants.

I've attached the spreadsheet and our draft estimate again. Marcus/Karthik — can you reply by EOD Friday with numbers we can share back to Liam? Monica, please prep the commercial estimate (term options + pilot pricing) after we lock the sizing.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: Thermogenix memory, KV routing, and quantization playbook

Naomi / team —

Quick technical repo of options; numbers are conservative and assume a 70B-class architecture similar to the ones in the catalog (per-layer KV scale and hidden-size assumptions). All numbers are per-replica working set estimates (weights + KV) and assume standard 32-bit pointers for KV indexing where applicable.

Option A — Sharded multi-GPU replica (preferred for critical low-latency):
- Hardware: 2x H100/A100 80GB NVLink pair per replica.
- Costs: higher infra footprint but gives lowest latency + no quantization quality hit.
- Memory estimates: float16 weights ~140GB split across 2 GPUs (~70GB each). KV at 32k ~12GB total -> partitioned across GPUs (~6GB each). Combined per-GPU: ~76GB (fits on 80GB).
- 90 concurrent sessions capacity (typical inference mix): provision 10 replicas (with 2x headroom for upgrades/burst -> 20 GPUs).

Option B — Single 80GB GPU + KV offload to NVMe (tradeoff balanced):
- Hardware: 1x 80GB GPU + high-throughput NVMe for KV page-in.
- Memory estimates: float16 weights + hot KV subset for 32k -> needs 1x 80GB if you offload cold KV pages. Effective latency impact varies; for sub-300ms SLO this works only if most hot prefixes are pre-warmed.
- Capacity: about 6–8K low-latency sessions per replica for short contexts; for your 32k tail, plan more replicas or aggressive caching.

Option C — Quantized single-GPU pool (cost-optimized, background tasks):
- Hardware: 1x 80GB GPU per replica (or lower-tier 48GB for highly quantized fits).
- Memory estimates: 4-bit weights ~35GB. KV at 32k ~12–14GB -> combined ~47–49GB, comfortably fits on 80GB and often on 48GB depending on KV implementation.
- Use for non-blocking summarization, batch jobs, and as explicit fallback.

Routing & rollout pattern (operational):
- Step 1: Canary float16 (5–10% of traffic) against production metrics (latency, quality evals from your prompt suite).
- Step 2: If within tolerance, shift low-risk routes to quantized pool and keep product-search pinned to float16 sharded replicas.
- Step 3: Maintain a warm pool of quantized replicas for overflow with automatic spillover rules.

Sizing recommendation for Thermogenix (initial pilot):
- Float16 sharded pool: 10 replicas (2x 80GB GPUs each) -> 20 x 80GB GPUs reserved.
- Quantized pool: 6 replicas (single 80GB GPUs) -> 6 x 80GB GPUs reserved.
- Autoscale headroom: reserve extra 20% capacity for burst.

I'll bake these numbers into the configuration doc and test the memory math on our in-house 32k KV trace. Marcus — if you agree, let's convert to a short slide and a formal Dedicated estimate for Monica to finalize terms.

—Karthik
